claims.text: An indexed query is not necessarily covered. Coverage means satisfying filtering and returned fields from index keys without fetching documents; a covered read has zero documents examined. (medium confidence)

A 2023 Percona forum reporter observed a large $or latency change when adding recurrence to the projection despite apparently equal plans and the same two branch indexes. The thread does not establish the root cause; compare the exact projected operations and execution statistics before attributing such a difference to index choice. (low confidence)

FETCH above IXSCAN can retrieve requested documents even when the index resolves the filter. A filter attached to FETCH identifies additional document-level predicate evaluation; FETCH alone does not prove residual filtering. (medium confidence)

Run find(filter).explain("executionStats") to examine the winning plan and its execution counters. Compare totalKeysExamined and totalDocsExamined with nReturned when assessing the work done for matching results. (medium confidence)

For sorted OR queries, distinguish merging ordered scans with SORT_MERGE from a separate SORT. SERVER-24027 illustrates that branch scan directions must provide compatible ordering for the merge; its reported scan-direction defect concerns MongoDB 3.2.3, not a demonstrated current limitation. (medium confidence)

IXSCAN establishes index use, not complete filter coverage or efficiency. FETCH reads collection documents and may apply residual filtering; compare totalKeysExamined and totalDocsExamined with nReturned instead of approving a plan from its stage names. (medium confidence)

Sorted indexed $or branches can use SORT_MERGE rather than an OR node followed by a blocking SORT. MongoDB's historical SERVER-51120 diagnosis explicitly identifies SORT_MERGE with IXSCAN children for such queries. (medium confidence)

For contained $or queries, common predicates can be distributed into branches. Indraneil Seal illustrates category AND (price OR quantity) and competing category/price and category/quantity indexes; inspect the chosen tree rather than inferring access paths from query syntax. (medium confidence)
An OR stage with multiple IXSCAN children in inputStages identifies indexed branch union. Read the whole tree: an enclosing FETCH or SUBPLAN can place OR below the root. (high confidence)

Compound indexes and union can coexist: Moratilla's example merges scans of owner_id/start_date and player_id/start_date indexes. Inspect each branch's indexName and indexBounds to determine which fields constrain that scan. (medium confidence)

The documented classic plan tree is directly under winningPlan; the slot-based engine exposes the logical tree under winningPlan.queryPlan and also emits slotBasedPlan. A reader must account for this structural difference. (low confidence)

executionStats describes completed winning-plan execution. allPlansExecution adds partial execution captured during candidate selection; those trial figures are not full executions of every rejected alternative. (low confidence)

In the documented indexed-OR tree, an OR stage has multiple IXSCAN children in inputStages. Moratilla’s example shows FETCH above OR with separate owner_id/start_date and player_id/start_date compound-index scans; compound indexes and branch union can coexist. (medium confidence)

Inspect every scan’s indexName, keyPattern, indexBounds and direction. These identify the index and scanned ranges; the presence of an IXSCAN alone does not show that every predicate constrained the scan. (medium confidence)

totalDocsExamined counts examinations, including filtered-out documents and repeated examinations of the same document; it is neither the result count nor necessarily a unique-document count. (low confidence)

Read winningPlan for the selected tree and rejectedPlans for alternatives. allPlansExecution adds partial trial statistics, which must not be treated as complete executions of every rejected candidate. (medium confidence)

Two IXSCAN children do not by themselves identify an OR union. SERVER-106829 records identical scans beneath AND_SORTED in a rejected candidate, illustrating why both the parent stage and candidate location matter. (medium confidence)

In Moratilla’s indexed-OR example, start_date has an unbounded descending interval while owner_id or player_id has an equality interval. The compound-index name therefore does not imply that start_date narrows the filter. (low confidence)
